input.quote: 7.2 Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives.
input.rationale: Section 7.2 imposes an MFN/right-to-match obligation on us as Customer: before engaging another provider we must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer we receive. It is unlimited as to product, term and comparison methodology, so it fails the fallback and sits in walk-away territory as an open-ended obligation to extend Vendor any better third-party terms. It also contradicts Section 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we made no exclusivity or most-favoured-customer commitment. No Vendor-granted MFN exists elsewhere to preserve. The narrowest cure is to negate the mandatory operator so no MFN obligation burdens Customer (preferred position).

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have negated the operator in Section 7.2 so that Customer need not disclose and match third-party offers: our playbook does not accept a most-favoured-nation or right-to-match obligation running against Customer, and this aligns with Section 12.3, where Vendor acknowledges we gave no exclusivity or most-favoured-customer commitment.
proposal.summary: Negate the mandatory operator in Section 7.2 to remove the Customer-side MFN/match obligation.
